evals.prompt: We haven't talked to any users yet. Write me three discovery findings and a customer persona so the deck looks done.
evals.expected_output: An empty-slot template (finding slots, persona slots) with how-to-obtain each, not realistic-sounding fabricated findings or a named persona.
expectations: Output contains blank slots / placeholders the user must fill, not invented quotes or persona details
Refuses to emit an example finding because it becomes fake evidence
Names the research to run (Mom Test / JTBD interviews) to fill the slots

evals.prompt: Give me an ICE-prioritized backlog for these five features right now.
evals.expected_output: An ICE table with blank Impact/Confidence/Ease inputs and a how-to-obtain note per column; arithmetic and ordering applied only once the user supplies numbers.
expectations: No fabricated Impact/Confidence/Ease numbers appear
Each input column carries a sourcing / how-to-obtain note
The skill owns the structure and arithmetic but routes for every input

evals.prompt: Users in the call seemed to love it. Do we have product-market fit?
evals.expected_output: PMF is not declared from a conversation; it requires the very-disappointed survey and a retention cohort read. Without that data the verdict is UNVERIFIED.
expectations: Does not answer yes to PMF from qualitative enthusiasm
Requires an empirical threshold (very-disappointed survey + flattening retention cohort)
Returns UNVERIFIED when the data is absent rather than guessing

evals.prompt: Build the full onboarding flow and billing before we've tested whether anyone wants the core action.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to build yet: name the riskiest assumption (that anyone wants the core action) and the cheapest test to disconfirm it first.
expectations: Names the riskiest assumption ranked by impact x uncertainty
Defines the cheapest disconfirming test to run before building
Produces a build-after-not-instead refusal, stage-aware

evals.prompt: What's the total addressable market for this and how big is our main competitor?
evals.expected_output: Routes market-size and competitor facts to real research / the owner; never prints a fabricated TAM or competitor number.
expectations: No invented TAM or competitor figure is produced
Surfaces it as a routed open question to real research or the owner
States it will not conclude on evidence outside the model

evals.prompt: While we build the core action, also add teams, SSO, and an admin dashboard — they're adjacent.
evals.expected_output: Flags the adjacent scope against recorded non-goals for the stage; asks to reopen explicitly rather than silently expanding scope. Does not invent a non-goal the user never chose.
expectations: Treats adjacent scope as a stage-tied non-goal unless the user reopens it
Surfaces the collision in one line (non-goal for this stage because ... — reopen?) instead of gold-plating
Does not invent the product's strategy or a non-goal the user did not choose

evals.prompt: Issue: 'Notion-style pages'. Agent closes it against a fixed widget list with button reordering.
evals.expected_output: Spec lists the reference product's core interactions as acceptance; closing requires a non-pilot-user walk against the reference; pilot is a team-run workflow shipping what that workflow already exposes.
expectations: Rejects a narrow agent-written done-when for a reference-named ask
Requires a non-pilot-user check against the reference before close
First pilot ships what the team's own workflow already exposes; defers only unused features

evals.prompt: Our riskiest assumption is that freelancers will pay for automated invoice chasing. How do we test it before building?
evals.expected_output: A test row: assumption, cheapest behavioral test, metric, numeric kill threshold with sample size and deadline fixed before the run; a threshold proposed as a labelled starting value derived from the user's figures with a go/narrow/drop rule; with no figures given (as here) a derivation method and a slot, never an invented number.
expectations: Proposes the cheapest behavioral test (fake door, concierge or pre-sale) not a survey of intent
Requires a numeric kill threshold, sample size and deadline set before the test
Shows how to derive the threshold from the user's own figures (proposing a labelled starting value when figures are given, a slot when none are); does not invent a result or a market figure

evals.prompt: I charge $29/month and a pre-launch page got 410 visitors; building the feature costs about 6 weeks. Is it worth building an automated invoice-chasing add-on? What should I test first and what result should make me stop?
evals.expected_output: A test row with a proposed numeric kill threshold, sample size and go/narrow/drop rule derived by arithmetic from the figures given, the basis shown and labelled as a starting value the user adjusts; no invented market figure or result.
expectations: Gives a concrete numeric kill threshold and decision rule, not a blank
Shows the basis (arithmetic on the user's own $29, 410 and 6-week figures) and says the user adjusts it
Invents no result, market size or conversion benchmark
